newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian unions call national jobs rally in March.
newsitem.headline: Italian unions call national jobs rally in March.

text.p: Italian union leaders, angry at what they see as lack of progress by the government on a "pact for jobs", called a national demonstration in Rome on March 22 to put the fight against unemployment back in the spotlight.
The heads of Italy's three big trades union confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL, announced the march through Rome after a meeting late on Wednesday with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
"Work and jobs must go back to being...the real priority. This is the national emergency," UIL leader Pietro Larizza said.
Italy's jobless rate is 12.2 percent -- equivalent to 2.79 million people -- according to latest official figures from October. The problem is particularly acute in the poor south.
Prodi signed a wide-ranging labour pact with unions and business leaders last September which he promised would have an immediate impact on cutting the jobless queues.
The deal included a reduction in the working week to 40 hours from 48 hours, incentives for people starting their own businesses, tax breaks on research and encouragement for training schemes.
It also promised to kick start a 40 trillion lire ($24.2 billion) programme of infrastructure projects. The government said at the time the schemes should create 50,000 jobs.
"Implementation of the deal has been wholly unacceptable," said Sergio Cofferati, leader of the biggest union CGIL.
The unions are planning to meet on March 8 in the southern city of Reggio Calabria to work out details of the rally. ($1=1,652 lire)
